newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares edge up, results offer support.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares edge up, results offer support.

text.p: The Nigerian stock market index inched higher on Thursday in dull trading, dealers said.
The all-share index closed 2.85 points up at 6746.46 against Wednesday's close of 6743.61.
"Except for the oil sector and a few other shares, there was not much interest in equities today," one trader said.
Two positive results helped to cheer the market.
An improved third quarter result saw the share price of Nigerian Breweries jump 20 kobo to 15.20 naira.
Turnover rose to 7,595 million naira in the period to end-September 1996 from 6,769 million naira in the same 1995 period. After-tax profit jumped to 925 million naira against 843 million naira.
Okomu Oil Palm rose 22 kobo to 6.70 naira on nine-month result showing pre-tax profit to end-September double to 84.3 million naira from 42.9 million naira in 1995.
But Van Leer Containers finished 10 kobo down at 12.55 naira on its declining half-year profit profile.
The gloom in the packaging sector persisted as Carnaud Metal Box ended two kobo lower at 3.06 naira and Studio Press was one kobo down at 81 naira.
Blue chips Lever Brothers tumbled 30 kobo to 22.50 naira on over-saturation of the market by its stock. The same reason cost Cadbury 10 kobo, dropping to 24.80 naira.
Ashaka Cement, down five kobo at 18.55 naira and Dunlop, 15 kobo lower at 10.30 naira, were the other big losers of the day.
Mobil Oil finished 30 kobo up at 45.30 naira, African Petroleum was 20 kobo higher at 40.20 naira and Unipetrol rose by the same figure to 51.60 naira.
AIICO Insurance closed at 9.70 naira, Nestle at 44.50 naira and West African Portland Cement Company at 40.30 naira, all 10 kobo better. ($1=80 naira)
